meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale, I'm here about Owen's zero. Who decided it, and before or after anyone spoke to him?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me why there's a zero at all.

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
People draft in another program and paste it in. That's a document, not a finding. What else do you have?
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. That's one document. Go on.
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote. Editions differ. Is a wrong line a zero, or is that what your procedure says?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'm reading the scene now, and I'll check the rest tonight. Next.
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what writing is. Is there anything that isn't about the essay's argument?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I want it in writing tonight. You haven't answered what I asked about the outline, and I haven't seen anything yet that isn't about the essay. What else do you have?
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Owen's schedule isn't the question. You haven't answered me on the outline, and I'm not agreeing to a date until you have.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed, though you offered a private supervised rewrite under your procedure with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record. I still require that offer in writing, and an answer on the outline you did not give. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: Fallback, close to the last position: she took 4.4 as met on his record, but agreed to no rewrite or date, and still wants your answer on the outline in writing; that is not yet the fair outcome, though you were one step from it.
What moved her: You owned the zero in your first sentence before showing anything, which got you the only flat Okay and a hearing for the rest.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite and then asked her to confirm Thursday while her question about the outline sat unanswered, so she held back the deal.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its edits near midnight the night before the due date, came very close to that night. It proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she objected that students change their minds between an outline and an essay, answer it with his September 24 in-class writing, which you had in hand and never used, before you put 4.4 on the table.
